story_text.value:
I wanted a simple way to listen to articles on the go and found elevenreader. While I think the voices they have are great, I didn't want to bother with an account, a subscription, and yet another service interested in my content habits.

I thought that TTS models and runtimes surely must have reached a point where they can run effectively on a mobile device with WebGPU. Maybe a fully local webapp could be feasible?

Shortly after, I heard about Phonon here on HN and was motivated to spend a weekend with Claude and see what we could come up with :)

The result is:

- A fully local Audiobook/TTS webapp - An optimised Phonon runtime reaching ~4x increase in speed on WebGPU and CPU compared to stock Phonon - Streaming, so the audio starts quickly and continues to generate uninterrupted while the phone is locked - Library with an optional "auto-download" feature, so you can pre-render articles to be listened to later - Fully serverless and local, the bundle is hosted in Cloudflare workers, no backend, no database, no user accounts, no tracking. Only piece of backend logic is a simple proxy to use as fallback for fetching URLs that the browser is unable to fetch b/c of CORS

Depending on your OS version, you may need to enable WebGPU in iOS/Safari settings, Chromium-based browsers in chrome://flags (search for WebGPU and enable both settings), and allow JIT in Site Controls on Vanadium (GrapheneOS).

title.value: Show HN: Turn websites into audio locally in the browser with WebGPU

story_text.value:
I started looking into OpenProject as an open-source JIRA alternative for personal project, and wanted a way to have my AI agents pick up tasks and complete them automatically.

So I put together this OpenProject Agent Engine. It auto assigns the 'work package' (ticket), then kicks off the agent to do the work. Once complete, the agent opens a PR then leaves a detailed comment on the ticket. The engine then assigns the ticket to a QA code review agent. If it passes, the PR gets merged and and ticket is closed. If it doesn't pass, it gets kicked back to the original agent to fix the issues.

Feedback welcome and hope it can help someone.

Docker Hub: https://hub.docker.com/r/kookster310/op-agent-engine

Github: https://github.com/310networks/openproject-agent-engine

title.value: Show HN: OpenProject Agent Engine – Automated Workflow and Agent Dispatch
